// PLANETARY DEFENSE COMMAND

TOTAL MOBILIZATION

EARTH STANDS · THE FLEET DESCENDS · HOLD THE LINE
TOTAL MOBILIZATION · v3.78.0 · CHANGELOG ▸ · 🏆 ACHIEVEMENTS · ▶ INTRO

CHANGELOG

// VERSION HISTORY

v3.78.0 — THE AFTER-ACTION DOSSIER
📖 The end-of-game report is now a multi-page dossier you can page through, download and share. A tab bar splits it into OVERVIEW (summary + graphs), ECONOMY (everything earned, spent, peaked, and produced), MILITARY (forces fielded vs lost, by domain, capitals, peak army), COMBAT (kills by enemy type, boss superweapons, strikes), RESEARCH & CONSTRUCTION (your doctrine timeline + everything you built), and WORLD. The World page shows two automatic snapshots of your planet — the fortress you built right before re-entry and the aftermath when it was over — alongside the combat heatmap. New ⬇ DOWNLOAD REPORT button saves the whole thing as a self-contained web page, and ⤴ SHARE posts your result. (More stat categories still to come — tell me which numbers you want.)

v3.77.0 — THE AFTER-ACTION REPORT KNOWS EVERYTHING
📊 The end-of-game screen now tracks the whole war. On top of the existing graphs and summary, you now get: FORCES FIELDED — every unit type you recruited, with its icon and a count; CONSTRUCTION — every building you raised; a RESEARCH TIMELINE showing which doctrines you unlocked and when; an expanded stat block with total IC / Manpower / Influence spent, peak army size, strikes launched, and your top kills by enemy type; and "WHERE THE WAR WAS FOUGHT" — a radar-style heatmap of the whole battlefield, from orbit down to the ground, lit up wherever the fighting was thickest. The whole report scrolls, so nothing gets cut off.

v3.76.0 — YOUR ANTI-MISSILE BATTERIES ACTUALLY WORK NOW
🎯 The Anti-Missile Interceptor is a true hit-to-kill weapon at last. Bunker-busters are tough by design (200 HP) so cheap flak can't casually swat them — but that toughness also meant your dedicated interceptor's round only chipped them, and a whole 4-round battery could barely kill one buster. A saturation barrage just walked through. Now a locked dedicated interceptor destroys any incoming penetrator in a single hit, so each battery is worth its whole magazine in kills and a layered anti-missile net can genuinely knock a barrage out of the sky. Generic flak (CIWS, Aegis) still can't one-shot a buster, so real anti-bombardment defense is still an investment — it just works when you make it. You can now hold the opening bombardment with conventional defenses; research and shields make it comfortable rather than mandatory.

v3.75.0 — RESEARCH IS CLICKABLE AGAIN (desktop fix)
🖱 Fixed: clicking a research node did nothing on PC. The doctrine tree grabbed your mouse pointer the instant you pressed down — which is what lets you drag to pan — but it did it too eagerly, stealing the click before it could ever reach the node, so you could click a node forever and nothing happened. Now the tree only grabs the pointer once you actually start dragging, so a plain click lands on the node and starts (or cancels, or queues) research like it should. Panning and pinch-zoom are unchanged.

v3.74.0 — THE INFANTRY HAVE FULLY LANDED
🪖 Squads no longer hover. The earlier grounding fix planted single vehicles correctly but missed squad units — they seated their soldiers using a small body-size value instead of the unit's real size, leaving every infantry squad floating a few pixels above the terrain (with their shadows floating too). Now squad bodies seat on exactly the same ground line as everything else, so infantry feet — and their shadows — sit flush on the dirt.

v3.73.0 — SQUADS LOOK LIKE SQUADS AT EVERY ZOOM
👥 No more "one soldier with squares floating over his head." When you're zoomed out, or once dozens of squads are on the field, the game draws each squad in a cheap simplified form to protect your framerate — but that form used to be a single soldier plus a row of little rectangle "strength pips," which read as confusing squares, not a squad. Now the simplified form draws a tight little cluster of soldiers instead, so a fireteam reads as a group at any zoom. The full detailed spread-out squad also stays on screen longer before it ever simplifies. (Purely visual — the one-brain-many-hitboxes squads fight exactly as before.)

v3.72.0 — SATELLITE HOUSEKEEPING
🛰 Your satellites hold station higher up, in the upper thermosphere just under the exosphere, instead of loitering low in the band. ⚙ Tungsten Rods sats stopped wasting rods on other satellites — a kinetic rod is a ground-bombardment weapon, so the Rods sat now only drops them on surface targets and enemies still in their vulnerable re-entry descent, never on things parked up in orbit at its own altitude. (Your Laser and Missile sats still engage space targets as before.)

v3.71.0 — YOU CAN ACTUALLY STOP THE BOMBARDMENT NOW
🛡 Bunker-busters drop 3 decoys, not 8. Your Anti-Missile Interceptor already ignored decoys, but the rest of your net (CIWS, Aegis) was drowning chasing bait while the real tungsten rods walked right in. Now the whole point-defense grid ruthlessly prioritizes real rods and busters over decoys — build layered air defense and you can genuinely knock a barrage down. ☄ The orbital plasma snipe is a real, physical shot you can intercept. It used to strike instantly with nothing to shoot at; now it's an actual plasma round that falls from orbit with travel time, and your point-defense can blast it out of the sky. 🪖 The magic flying infantry have landed. Ground units were rendering a few pixels above the terrain — now their feet and tracks sit flush on the ground. 👥 Squads read as squads. A fireteam's members were drawing scattered — one floating, one sunk — reading as a jumbled dark blob; now they stand together in their own shadows as a coherent unit (a visual fix only — the one-brain-many-hitboxes behavior is unchanged).

v3.70.0 — THE CAPITAL FLEET GETS A FACE
🛠️ All five Grand Arsenal capital ships now have their own bespoke artwork. Until now they were secretly borrowing basic units' sprites just scaled up — the "Mobile Command Fortress" was literally drawn as a little AA flak gun, the Land Dreadnought was a regular tank. Now each is a proper capital-class machine, drawn to match what it actually does: the Land Dreadnought is a tracked land-battlefort with a hull-length spinal railgun; the Grand Battleship is a three-turret dreadnought with a command tower; the Super Carrier is a long flush-deck arsenal flattop; the War Colossus is a twin-cannon walking strider; and the Mobile Command Fortress is a citadel on treads with a comms mast, a visible garrison, and its command-aura ring. All still aim, walk and face exactly as before — only the silhouette changed. (The regular tanks, carrier and Colossus Walker are untouched.)

v3.69.0 — DOCTRINE PATHS REDRAWN
🧬 Superhumans are now the far end of the shield path, not an early bio pick. Engineered demigods need a personal deflector field to survive what they're built to fight, so Superhumans now requires Biotechnology and Miniaturized Shielding — it sits much deeper in the tree, at a real cost, as the payoff it always should have been. 🦿 Living Titans decoupled: the Titan superweapon used to hang off Superhumans, which would have dragged it behind the whole shield chain — it now grows straight out of the Cloning Vats, staying a pure Bioengineering path you can reach without detouring through Defense.

v3.68.0 — CAPITAL SHIPS ARE WALKING FORTRESSES
🛡️ Every Grand Arsenal super-heavy now carries a personal shield and fires three independent weapon systems at once — a main gun, a dedicated anti-air turret, and its own close-in flak — so one of these is a mobile defense network, not a single big cannon. And each finally has a distinct role instead of being the same ship at different sizes: the Land Dreadnought out-ranges everything on the ground but is blind to high air; the Grand Battleship is a naval bombardment platform that reaches any altitude; the Super Carrier is lightly armed itself but fights through its 8-plane air wing behind the toughest shield; the War Colossus is a line-breaker whose plasma cannon shreds whole clusters (no longer just "a bigger Colossus"); and the Mobile Command Fortress is a command-and-control anchor with the heaviest shield of all. Upkeep nudged up to match — these are the apex of total mobilization, and they cost like it.

v3.67.0 — SQUADS THAT FIGHT LIKE SQUADS
👥 Your fireteams are finally real. Squad units (infantry, drone swarms, fighter flights) used to look like one blob that died all at once — now they hold a loose, visibly-separate formation of individual soldiers that shuffle and flex as they move, each with their own body and shadow. 💀 They die one at a time. The real bug: every explosion, firestorm, quake and beam — the game's main source of damage — was draining a squad's shared health pool and then popping the whole formation at once, while only direct rifle fire hit individual bodies. Now all damage lands on the soldiers nearest the blast: a stray round drops one man, a direct shell takes a few, and only overwhelming fire wipes the whole team. A squad grinds down like a real unit instead of vanishing in a puff.

v3.66.0 — THE EXPLOSIONS ARE BACK (and your air force learned restraint)
💥 Fixed the muted explosions. A perf guard from the death-effects update was stripping the smoke, shrapnel and screen-shake off every kill the moment a battle passed 200 units — which in a real late-game fight is always. The threshold's now way up, and conventional gun/missile/plasma kills are as loud and messy as they should be again — while lasers still melt units to sludge and antimatter still annihilates. 🎯 Fire discipline — the big one. Your fighters no longer empty their entire missile stockpile at one lone drone: they commit a shot or two, then hold and reassess. In testing that cut missiles-fired-at-one-drone from ~40 down to ~3. They also stop chasing orbital enemies they can't hit (and dying for free doing it), and your own satellites now hold station in the thermosphere. 🚁 Helicopters are the right size (they were bigger than jets), and fighter missiles are much smaller so an air battle isn't a wall of missile sprites. 🔬 Research: "War Walkers" is now Super-Heavy Ground Units, the capstone of the Robotics path, and the Grand Arsenal is unlocked there (and finally listed in the node). 📋 Menus now show upkeep on anything that has it, and the total component cost of a production batch.

v3.65.0 — MISSILES RUN OUT OF FUEL
🚀 Missiles now have finite motor burn. Every missile lights its motor, accelerates for a few seconds, then the engine cuts out — the flame dies and it coasts the rest of the way on momentum and gravity, seeker barely steering. It looks right (you can see the burn end), it stops missiles chasing forever and eating the frame budget, and a missile that can't reach its target now burns out and falls instead of climbing into space. Burn times are tuned per type — a snappy short burn on fighter missiles, a long hot run on the hypervelocity interceptors. 🎯 And the micromissile ground-dive is fixed — submunitions no longer auger straight into the dirt the instant they split off their carrier; they kick up and out before the seeker takes over.

v3.64.0 — DISCIPLINED INTERCEPTORS & TIDIER MENUS
☢ The Anti-Missile Interceptor is now a precision asset, not a spammer. It holds a tighter 4-round magazine and reloads slower (~10s) — but it now holds its fire and prioritizes the real threats: it saves rounds for incoming tungsten rods and bunker-busters, completely ignores decoys, and won't waste a shot on a minor target. 🖱 The production menu stops fighting you — bumping a unit's quantity no longer snaps your scroll back to the top. 🏭 And you can finally see what your factories make — select any garrison or production building and its panel now spells out exactly what it produces or supplies to the area.

v3.63.0 — REAL FIRETEAMS
🪖 Squads move like a real fireteam now — one mind, many bodies. Each soldier in a squad is its own body with its own position and hitbox, held to the group by a spring-like cohesion so they cluster tight and flex naturally instead of moving as one rigid blob. A shell that lands on the left of a squad hits the man on the left, not an abstract center point. But the squad still thinks with one brain — it picks its target and makes its decisions once, and the soldiers act on it together — so it's smarter and costs no more to run (we actually cut some wasted work: riflemen used to each re-scan for targets independently, and now they share the squad's). Purely how squads move and take hits — no stat changes.

v3.62.0 — BOOTS ON THE GROUND
🥾 Ground units now actually sit on the ground. Tanks, infantry and the rest were rendering with a small gap under them — their treads and feet floating a little above the terrain. They're seated flush now, on flat ground and on slopes, with their health bars, selection boxes and muzzle flashes all following them down. Purely a visual seating fix — nothing about how they move, aim or take cover changed.

v3.61.0 — DIE BY THE WEAPON
💀 Units now die according to what killed them — more than ever. Get hit by a laser and you don't explode, you melt — the body slumps and settles into a glowing molten puddle that cools and crusts over, hissing steam. Nanite rounds disassemble a target into a scatter of cold motes instead of blasting it. Antimatter annihilates — a brilliant flash and an inward-collapsing shockwave that leaves almost nothing behind. (Guns still riddle, missiles still tumble, plasma still spalls, railguns still cleave.) Also fixed a bug where nanite kills were mistakenly playing the laser death effect. All cosmetic, and it dials itself back when the battlefield is already a chaotic mass.

v3.60.0 — A WORLD WORTH DEFENDING
🌆 The world feels alive now. Between the mountains sit distant towns with lit windows; civilian cars run the roads between your cities, boats drift on the water, and the occasional airliner crosses high overhead trailing a contrail. And then the fleet arrives — and everyone runs. The moment re-entry is detected, the cars scatter and speed off, the boats make for shore, the planes divert, and the town windows go dark. On the far horizon during the invasion you can see the wider war you're only glimpsing a slice of: drop pods streaking down in the distance and far-off defensive batteries firing back. None of it is anything you control or fight — it's the planet you're actually defending, living and then fleeing. (All cosmetic, and cheap.)

v3.59.0 — AIRLIFT
🚁 A new Transport Helicopter "Chinook" that ferries your rear troops to the front — automatically, no micromanaging. Build one and it just works: it finds units sitting idle far behind the fighting, flies out, picks them up, and drops them near the front — crossing water and terrain your rail tunnels can't. It's the air version of the Rail Hub. Units in the air are safe cargo (they can't fire or be hit while aboard), and if a loaded transport is shot down, its passengers are set down safely rather than lost. Pure logistics: get your muster to the battle faster.

v3.58.0 — TANKS TAKE TO THE WATER
🌊 Reach the Fusion Age and your tracked armor becomes amphibious. Once you research the Fusion Age, your tanks, heavies, artillery, MLRS, Mammoths and the new land capital hulls all get advanced drive systems: they're ~40–50% faster and they drive straight across water like it's solid ground, instead of being walled off at the shoreline. It's the long-standing fix for ground forces feeling stuck on one strip of land — now they can flank across rivers and seas and hit the beachheads from angles they never could. (Before Fusion, and for infantry, nothing changes — deep water still stops them.)

v3.57.0 — YOUR ARMY FIGHTS SMARTER
🧠 Units now leverage their advantages instead of throwing themselves forward. Four changes, all behavior — no stats touched: Ranged units hold their range — fragile long-reach units (artillery, MLRS, SAMs, the Arsenal Ship) settle at the edge of their own weapon range and kite back if something closes on them, instead of marching into point-blank to die. Fire is smarter — your guns bias toward the most dangerous reachable target (a landed superweapon, a bomber about to drop) rather than just the nearest, while still spreading out so they don't all dogpile one thing. ★ Your air force masses up — idle fighters now gather into a wing and commit together rather than trickling in one at a time to be picked off; an urgent threat still scrambles them immediately. And badly-hurt, unsupported units fall back toward friendly strength instead of feeding themselves in. Tanks and short-range brawlers still charge in as before. (New AI behavior — tell me how it feels; every threshold is tunable.)

v3.56.1 — small fix
Fixed a harmless-but-noisy rendering error thrown by shrinking explosion particles during heavy orbital bombardment (a particle's radius could briefly dip below zero and upset the canvas). Purely cosmetic plumbing — no gameplay change.

v3.56.0 — HOLD THE LINE
🛡 Apocalypse is an endurance run now, not a slow-motion loss. In the Apocalypse scenario the fleet never lands — it just glasses your cities from orbit until it runs dry, so you can only survive. The old readout counted up a demoralizing "survived 9%." Now it's an honest objective: ENDURANCE — HOLD FOR a target, with your survival time and a saved personal best right there in the HUD. Outlast the fleet's orbital ordnance and you win outright — "YOU HELD THE LINE." Every other scenario is unchanged; Apocalypse is now a last stand you chase a record on.

v3.55.0 — TWO SHIPS, TWO JOBS
🚢 The Missile Cruiser and the Arsenal Ship are no longer near-twins. The Missile Cruiser is now a dedicated fleet air-defense escort — guided interceptor missiles with enormous reach (all the way to orbit) plus a close-in autocannon that swats incoming ordnance; it protects the fleet, it doesn't slug it out with the ground. The Arsenal Ship "Leviathan" leans all the way into VLS saturation — longer reach and faster salvos of surface-attack rockets — but its own air defense is now thin, so it wants a Cruiser (or air cover) riding shotgun. Two ships that now actually want to sail together.

v3.54.0 — FASTER UNDER LOAD
⚡ Another big performance pass — the late-game update loop is ~40% cheaper. At a full battlefield (hundreds of units, hundreds of enemies, ~700+ shells in the air) the per-frame simulation cost dropped by roughly a third. Under the hood: the friendly/enemy/target lists that combat scans were being rebuilt from scratch once per unit and once per projectile, every single frame — now they're computed once per frame and shared; the dead-unit cleanup no longer rebuilds five whole arrays every frame; the friendly separation pass uses the same fast distance-bucketing the enemies already had; and the HUD text refreshes at a calmer rate. Zero gameplay change — it just runs smoother on a phone when the screen is full of war.

v3.53.0 — GROUND & SEA CAPITAL SHIPS
🏗 The sky isn't the only place you get giants now. A new Grand Arsenal building (unlocked at the Space Age) assembles a whole tier of screen-scale ground and naval capital units — the counterpart to the Sky Fortresses. Five of them, each a distinct role: the Land Dreadnought (a rolling siege battleship with a long-range railgun), the Grand Battleship (naval shore bombardment that out-ranges an orbital rod), the Super Carrier "Leviathan-class" (eight fighter wings off one deck), the War Colossus (a giant mech bruiser above the Titan), and the Mobile Command Fortress (a command bastion on treads that rolls a big fire-rate + range aura across the front). Like the sky warships they sit off the army cap and carry a heavy standing upkeep — you can field a fleet of them, but your economy will feel it. (This is a first draft — tell me how they feel.)

v3.52.0 — OVERWATCH & HONEST TOOLTIPS
🚁 New Command Helicopter "Overwatch" — a support rotorcraft that carries no real teeth but projects a mobile command aura: friendly units near it fire +20% faster and reach +12% farther, like a flying Ammo Depot and Radar in one. It loiters over the front on its own, so the buff follows the fighting — park it over your main push. Draws Rotor Command like your other helicopters. 📝 And a big honesty pass on the tech-tree descriptions: several research nodes were under-selling themselves — Nanotech now lists its Nanite Foundry & Turret, Telekinesis names its Tractor Beam, Directed Energy names the Laser Plane, Plasma names the Plasma Bastion Works, and a few over-claims (helicopters getting plasma, all resources softening strike costs) were corrected. What the tree says it gives you is now what it actually gives you.

v3.51.0 — STABILITY IS FOR ATROCITIES
☢ Strategic strikes no longer all cost stability. Paying political capital to lob a big conventional missile never made sense — that's just artillery. So conventional strikes (Heavy Guided Missile, Kinetic Lance, Micromissile Barrage, Combat Drop) now cost only IC + a cooldown, no stability at all. The stability cost is reserved for the genuinely unthinkable — Nuclear, Cluster MIRV, Firestorm, Antimatter, and the Mind-Forge. Now spending stability actually means something: it's the price of an atrocity, not the price of ordnance.

v3.50.0 — LOCAL GARRISON WORKS
🏭 A new way to defend: buildings that garrison the ground AROUND them. Plant a Local Garrison Works in your sprawl and it steadily manufactures its specialty and divvies the fresh units out to whatever you've built nearby — so your defense grows out of your industry, not a menu. Five of them, all in the INFRASTRUCTURE tab, all no-research: Missile Works (rocket batteries), Heavy Foundry (Mammoth super-heavies), Aero Works (fighter screen + +4 Air Command + unlocks the Lancer bomber & Laser Plane), Armor Plate Mill (heavy tanks), and Avionics Works (guided SAMs). They stack — build more, overlap their radii, and the local area fills with defenders; the only ceiling is your Garrison Stockpile budget, so if you want a bigger standing army, build more Stockpiles. Placement matters: one dumped underground in the middle of the ocean garrisons nothing — build them into your lines. Turn on coverage zones (V) to see each one's radius. Veterans' Hall moved into Infrastructure alongside them, and the old production-line units (Hydra, Mammoth, Lancer, Solaris) are buildable from any factory again once their works stands.

v3.49.0 — CLEAN MENUS & A REAL INTERCEPTOR
🧭 The build menu can't overflow the screen anymore. The SPEC and INFRA tabs were rendering a full description under every card, which made those lists so tall they pushed the tab row off the top of the screen — so at large UI scale you couldn't click away to another tab. Cards are now compact (hover any card to read what it does), and long tabs scroll internally, so the menu always stays on screen and every tab stays reachable. 🚀 The Anti-Missile Interceptor is finally worth its slot — and a third of the price. It cost 1500 IC and fired a missile that crawled at normal speed and missed; now it costs 500 IC and LEAPS a big hypervelocity hit-to-kill interceptor off the rail — the fastest missile in the game (~5× a normal one), with a hard-tracking seeker and a proximity fuse so it airbursts on a near miss instead of tunnelling past. It still holds a finite magazine of 6 and reloads slowly: it defends a sector, it doesn't shrug off a saturation barrage.

v3.48.2 — HOTFIX: RESEARCH IS NEVER LOCKED
🔧 Fixed research (and strikes) refusing to open after the tutorial. The onboarding used to hard-block the RESEARCH and STRIKE buttons until it decided your economy was ready — and if that unlock milestone never fired, you could be stranded with no way into the tree at all, even with labs, influence and the right tech. Now the tutorial only advises you to wait; it never stops you. Click RESEARCH whenever you like and it opens — you'll just get a gentle "might want to build up first" nudge if it's early.

v3.48.1 — SMALL FIXES
◣ The RESEARCH button now shows a progress bar — a thin purple fill along the bottom tracks how far your active research has been funded, so you can watch it fill without opening the tree. 🚀 The "Ballistic Missile" strike is now the "Heavy Guided Missile" — it was never ballistic (it flies to the target under its own thrust, not on a gravity arc), so the name finally matches what it actually does.

v3.48.0 — READ THE BATTLEFIELD
🗺 The corner minimap is rebuilt. It no longer squashes the whole 6,000-wide world into a useless thin smear — it draws the sky as stacked altitude layers, so at a glance you can tell whether a threat is a ground landing, a stratosphere bomber, or something parked in orbit (which tells you which weapons can even reach it). Bosses show as diamonds, there's a frontline line, a legend, and camera-scrub still works. ⊕ Global Fire Control — a corner ⊕ button (key F) lights up every gun and unit's reach as coverage rings across the whole field, and lets you click anywhere to designate targets your whole defense grid will prioritize — no more selecting one emplacement at a time. 🏛 Six new home-front buildings: War Academy (veterancy damage aura), Field Hospital (repair aura, no research needed), Logistics Hub (cuts your standing upkeep), Veterans' Hall (fields the new elite Veteran Guard), Fortress HQ (a fortified garrison anchor), and Industrial Combine (income + faster, cheaper construction). 🪖 Smarter idle units — units with nothing to shoot no longer stand around: ground forces march to the front, ships patrol their coast, and idle fighters drift toward the fight — but a unit garrisoning a building or city holds its post instead of chasing a distant incursion across the map.

v3.47.0 — SMOOTHER & TIDIER
⚡ Big performance boost — the late-game slog runs roughly 3× faster now. Anything off-screen is no longer drawn, glows and tracers are cached instead of rebuilt every frame, and heavy detail dials back only when the field is already a chaotic mass — so it looks the same, just far smoother on a phone. ☢ The strike panel finally closes (there's an × now), and — crucially — you can launch strikes even when your stability is on the floor. No more being locked out of your missiles during the exact crisis where you need them; a "desperation launch" just drains what stability you have left. ⚑ The allies menu grew to 8 packages (interceptors, artillery, helicopters, bombers, heavy armor…). 🏭 The production menu is rebuilt — compact, split into tabs by type, with a side panel showing each unit's description, weapons (including research upgrades) and full cost, and a ×N stepper to queue a batch at once. 💡 A new TIP button serves quick advice for new commanders. 🏙 And your cities recruit for you — surviving cities muster a trickle of manpower and the occasional militia, unless they're under siege.

v3.46.0 — BACKLOG SWEEP II
⚙ Your capital ships now upgrade with your research. Research Plasma Weapons and their gun batteries become plasma; research Particle Beams and the Railgun Ship's spinal cannon becomes a near-hitscan particle beam — the apex atmospheric weapon (antimatter stays space-only, because firing it in air would annihilate you). A new Miniaturized Shielding doctrine gives every capital ship a rechargeable deflector shield, and your naval warships now fight with a main gun and a dedicated AA turret. 🏛 You inherit a nation now — cities start with garrisons, factories and a few missile silos instead of bare dirt. ⚑ Allied reinforcements surge in to help if you're caught badly underprepared. And a new ⚑ ALLIES button lets you spend banked Influence to call in a Carrier Strike Group, an Armored Battalion, or an Air Wing — a real use for a full influence bar.

v3.45.0 — BACKLOG SWEEP I
🚁 Two new helicopters: the Scout Heli "Kestrel" (fast, light, hunts enemy aircraft with air-to-air missiles) and the heavy gunship "Mastodon" (big, tanky, a real Rotor-Command investment). 🎯 The Aegis Battery is smart now — instead of the same dumb flak stream as the CIWS, it fires sleek cyan GUIDED interceptors that home in and chase down incoming missiles and rods. 🗺 Better maps — no more "Waterworld" rolls where the whole map is ocean and everything crams into one mega-city; there's always a decent coastline now, and cities spread out along it. ☢ And a secret: there may be consequences to reaching for the nuclear option before the enemy even arrives. Do try to find out.

v3.44.0 — CARRIERS, KITING & FLAK
🛥 Carriers actually carry aircraft now. They were dribbling out one plane every ~20 seconds from an empty deck, so under fire they always looked empty — now a carrier launches its whole wing at once and replaces losses fast, so the Nanoforge and naval carriers finally fight like carriers. ✈ Your aircraft stop committing suicide. Missile jets now use their range: they hold back near the edge of their reach and fling ordnance from a distance instead of diving into a fortress full of point-defense. 🛡 Every capital ship now has its own point-defense. All the sky warships and naval warships run built-in CIWS that swats a couple of incoming missiles out of the air each moment — so they can actually survive the missile-saturated frontline instead of melting. (No explosion-spam — just clean tracers.)

v3.43.0 — SURVIVING THE COLLAPSE
⚖ The Capitulation Crisis no longer flip-flops you to death. When your cities were being overrun, stability could get pinned at 0 and the game would spam "CRISIS! …never mind. CRISIS! …never mind" every second, with no way to climb out no matter how many Comms Towers you built — miserable. Now a crisis is a real, recoverable setback: it hits once (troops mutiny, production freezes), then the government forcibly stabilizes — your stability is guaranteed to climb back to fighting shape over a few seconds (the drains that caused the collapse are held off while it recovers), and a grace period stops it from immediately re-triggering. The banner now shows your recovery progress. You only actually LOSE if the nation collapses several times over — a sustained failure, not a single bad moment.

v3.42.0 — THE SKY FLEET
🛸 A whole new tier of capital ships takes to the air. Build a Sky Dock and, once you've researched Sky Fortresses, you can field five sleek anti-grav sky warships: the Patrol Ship (cheap picket), the Destroyer (rapid AA escort), the Missile Cruiser (long-range VLS), the Railgun Ship (a spinal railgun that reaches all the way to orbit), and the Nanoforge Carrier — a self-repairing flagship that launches jets and helicopters from its deck. They cruise the atmosphere as a class of their own — they don't take hangar slots, and they're a serious investment. This is Phase 1: the fleet flies and fights. Next, its weapons will start upgrading as you research (particle cannons, lasers, shields, drone bays…) so each ship becomes a living readout of your whole tech tree.

v3.41.0 — YOUR AIR FORCE CAN AIM NOW
✈ Fighters were genuinely broken — now fixed. Whole fighter wings were firing dumb, non-tracking missiles at a single point in an enemy formation and ignoring everything else. Now each fighter picks its own target, the wing spreads its fire across the enemy instead of dogpiling one spot, they stop clumping into a stack, and their missiles actually home and airburst near a target instead of needing a perfect direct hit. 👾 The Bombardier got reined in: its point-defense (which was swatting most of your fire out of the sky) is roughly halved, its numbers of escort satellites trimmed — and a real bug is fixed where its laser-defense satellites could snipe your units clear across the entire map; their range is now hard-capped to their local area. It's still oppressive — it's supposed to be — but beatable.

v3.40.1 — CLEAN SIDES
The screen-edge vignette was made even earlier but never actually made subtle — on wide screens you could still see the sides darkening. Now the darkening only touches the far corners as a faint frame, and the side edges stay clear (measured: ~9.6% side-darkening → ~1.4%). Still fully removable via the Film Grain & Vignette toggle in Options.

v3.40.0 — NEW WINGS
✈ The whole player jet roster got redrawn. The Falcon, Wraith, Solaris, Warthog, Reaper and Warden are all new sprites now — sleeker near-future silhouettes with clean symmetric wings (no more lopsided planes), edge glow, and a distinct outline each so you can tell them apart at a glance. First step of a broader art glow-up bringing the older units up to the standard of the new capital-ship designs.

v3.39.0 — ROTORS UP
🚁 Helicopters are their own arm now. They don't compete with your jets for hangar space — they run on a separate ROTOR COMMAND pool, filled by cities and the new Heli-Depot building, so a cheap chopper and an expensive fighter no longer fight over the same slot. They need no runways — they base and rearm at cities, depots, or any carrier deck. They fly a totally different way: low-altitude close air support — they close on a target, hover over it and hose it down, drifting along with it, instead of making fast strafing passes like jets. They're deliberately capped to low altitude (they can't reach high-flying enemies — that's what your railguns and interceptors are for). 🛥 And your carriers now launch a gunship helicopter alongside their fighter wing — "helicopter carrier" is real, and the future sky flagships will lean into it hard.

v3.38.1 — AIRCRAFT FIRE UP, DON'T FLY UP
Correction to the last update: aircraft now reach into the thermosphere with their weapons but physically cruise no higher than the mesosphere — they engage the band above them without climbing into it. (The exosphere is still space-weapons-only.)

v3.38.0 — INTERCEPT & AFTER-ACTION
🛡 A real answer to orbital bombardment: the Anti-Missile Interceptor battery. A dedicated defensive building that hunts incoming bunker-busters, tungsten rods and missiles with homing interceptors and — unlike your aircraft — reaches all the way to space to catch them on descent. The catch: it holds only 6 interceptors and reloads slowly, one at a time. It can't stop a saturation barrage by itself — you invest in several and still have to triage what to save. ✈ Aircraft fly one band higher now — the hard mesosphere ceiling was walked back up into the thermosphere (the exosphere stays space-only). 📊 The after-action report grew its graphs — the end screen now charts your economy, stability, your forces vs the enemy's, and the autofleet's decline over the whole match, so you can see exactly how the battle turned. Plus a few description fixes for units that named buildings that no longer exist.

v3.37.0 — THE FLEET SPREADS OUT
🌍 The invasion no longer politely trickles into one spot. The moment orbital bombardment opens, five bombarders now fan out across the entire width of the map — plasma pressure on every stretch of ground from the first second, not one predictable lane. 📈 Landings snowball if you ignore them: leave a flank unanswered and the next drop there comes in bigger — and bigger — up to a hard cap, while crushing a landing shrinks it back. Punish neglect. ⚠ Every super-unit announces itself now — the groundfall/on-station warning banner used to fire only for the Land Leviathan; now Skyfortresses, Bombarders, Annihilators and Harvesters all call out when they arrive, so nothing sneaks in. (This escalation is deliberately tuned on the gentle side for now — feedback welcome.) 🛠 Plus quality-of-life: dug-in units no longer block you from building on their spot · click again to reach a building hidden behind a unit · special-building effects now show in both the SPEC and Infrastructure menus · and selecting a factory shows what it's producing, how fast, and its garrison.

v3.36.0 — SMOOTHER, LEANER, SHARPER
⚡ Big performance fix for the wall-of-guns lag. Rapid-fire guns (especially CIWS) were spawning a full impact explosion on every single round — thousands of pointless effects per second melting phones. Those per-round booms are gone: the bright tracer streak is the hit now, and the guns kill exactly as well as before. Tracers themselves are also thinner and smaller, like real ones. 🏰 The free foxhole guns are no longer a god-wall. The auto-emplacements your dug-in infantry throw up (MG nests, flak, field guns) hit for about half as much, half as fast — still a strong line, but a heavy or saturating enemy can now push through instead of dissolving on contact. 🗡 The Titan finally fights like one — its embarrassing machine gun is replaced by a spinal plasma siege cannon (one earth-shaking slug, not bullet spray). 🧹 Tree cleanup: cut three dead stat-only research nodes (Mass Drivers, Void Engine, Hive Mind) and the Scout that scouted nothing, and fixed the Nanotech node so it actually tells you it unlocks the Nanite Foundry & Nanite Turret.

v3.35.0 — LEARN IT ONE PIECE AT A TIME
🎓 A rebuilt HOW TO PLAY that stops drowning you. The most common complaint about this game is that it's genuinely hard to learn — so the tutorial no longer throws all 55 buildings and 28 doctrines at you at once. It now teaches in phases: at the start, Research and Strikes are greyed out on purpose and your only job is industry — Power Plants and Extractors on resource nodes. Once your economy is actually standing on its feet, the next layer unlocks with a word on research (build a couple of Labs first!), and strikes light up as re-entry nears. 💬 And a new ADVISOR quietly reads your economy and nudges you — hoarding Influence? Go research. Out of Manpower? Build Housing or lean on machines. Stability slipping? Ease off and raise your cap. It points a direction and shows you the ways; it never forces your hand. Fully skippable, and replayable any time from the menu.

v3.34.0 — ENEMY SHIELDS WORK NOW
🛡 Enemy shields finally block your fire. The autodrones' beachhead shield domes were quietly letting your plasma and every splash weapon walk straight through — a "shield" that did nothing. Now an enemy dome absorbs your incoming fire (plasma splash included) and drains under sustained pressure, exactly the way YOUR Shield Generator blocks theirs. Beams and strategic strikes still punch through — that's what they're for. ✈ New aircraft — Laser Interceptor "Warden": anti-missile point-defense lasers moved off the multirole Fighter (a fighter hauling a PD laser was always a stretch) onto a dedicated interceptor. Fighters keep their missiles; the Warden holds the sky against incoming ordnance.

v3.33.0 — THE FLEET MEANS IT NOW
The invasion got serious. 👾 Every landing brings a super-unit — in GROUPS. No more lone bosses; 2–3 arrive together, each a mobile CARRIER that keeps fabricating fresh squads, and each reinforces if you don't kill it within ~30 seconds. 💥 The Bombardier is oppressive now: on arrival it deploys TEN railgun satellites and TEN laser-defense satellites, brings a SUPPORT SHIP that repairs everything around it, fires its point-defense twice as fast, and snipes your GROUND units with an orbital plasma cannon (it can't touch aircraft — so keep some of your force airborne). 🎯 Smarter landings: the fleet scouts for your WEAKEST, least-defended stretch and drops THERE — fewer, heavier waves instead of a predictable trickle. 🚀 Tougher decoys: the bunker-buster decoy screen now takes several hits to clear, so picking out the real penetrators is harder.

v3.32.1 — WHAT'S BUFFING THIS UNIT?
⚡ Select a unit and the info panel now shows its ACTIVE BUFFS — every aura on it (Radar range, Ammunition Depot fire-rate, Nanite Foundry repair) with the buildings responsible, and an explicit "STACKED N×" callout so you can finally SEE that ringing a gun with support buildings multiplies its power. Also lists your research doctrine bonuses, era-upgrade status, and production discounts. No more guessing why one turret is a god.

v3.32.0 — MEDALS & A COUP
🏆 New achievements — including "Who Needs Science?" (win a game having researched absolutely nothing), "This Will Have No Long-Term Consequences" (10 nuclear strikes in one game), "Oops" (launch a nuke during peacetime), "I Forgot to Research" (20 ballistic strikes in one game), and "Regime Change." 🏛 The coup screen: if your stability collapses BEFORE the invasion even arrives, you weren't beaten in battle — your own government overthrew you. The defeat now says so: A COUP — your own state removed you before the enemy ever arrived.

v3.31.1 — THE DARK EDGES, EXPLAINED
🖼 The weird dark zones on the sides of the screen are fixed. Two vignettes were stacking, and the main one built its bright "safe zone" as a circle sized off the screen's SHORTER side — so on a wide phone screen the entire left and right margins fell into heavy shadow while the top and bottom escaped. Now there's exactly ONE vignette, a true screen-shaped ellipse, softened into a quiet even frame. The Film Grain & Vignette accessibility toggle still clears it completely. 🌙 And a secret: the moody dark-edged look survives as a deliberate experiment — a hidden NIGHT MODE prototype (off by default) that leans into deep, cool framing on purpose.

v3.31.0 — GUNS THAT HIT, SQUADS THAT DON'T DROWN
⚡ Particle Cannons are true hitscan. They were firing a hyper-fast projectile that flew past fast targets ("9000 stars, zero hits"). Now it's an instant beam that strikes the same tick — a real lance of light. Ring one with Ammo Depots for the wall of light it was meant to be. 🎯 Every gun leads its shots. All projectile weapons — rifles, flak, tanks, railguns, bombers, even city militia — now aim where the target will be, using a corrected intercept solve (measured 0% → 100% hit rate on fast crossing targets). Beams and particle cannons are instant, so they don't need to lead. 🪖 Infantry squads: prettier, cheaper, and they stop drowning. Squads redrawn as a clean staggered fireteam instead of an overlapping smear; trimmed to 3 bodies with a level-of-detail render so a huge army stays smooth on your phone instead of grinding to a halt. And ground units no longer shove each other into the sea — a drowned unit sinks quietly instead of exploding.

v3.30.1 — DEFINED ROLES
🏛 Comms vs. Propaganda have distinct jobs now. The Comms Tower is THE stability-reserve building — the only structure that banks a shock-absorber reserve (and it's stronger now that it's the specialist). The Propaganda Bureau is THE stability-cap building — it lifts your ceiling harder than anything else, and no longer banks a reserve. Build both, for different reasons. 📡 Radars stack: the Radar description now tells you what was always true — ring a heavy gun with several Radars to reach dramatically farther.

v3.30.0 — SQUADS TAKE THE FIELD
🛩 Drones and fighters fight as squads now. Combat drones deploy as 3-body swarms, and your 6th-gen Fighter finally flies with its actual Loyal-Wingman escorts — one crewed Falcon leading two pilotless drones, each with its own weapon. (Wingmen have never actually appeared before; now they do.) 🎨 Distinct craft: the kamikaze drone and the loyal-wingman are no longer the same sprite — kamikaze is a finned dart with a glowing warhead, the wingman a twin-tail stealth jet. 🐛 Squad exploit fixed: producing infantry, drones or fighters was quietly giving you six / three / two squads per order at the price of one — now one order buys exactly one squad, one army-cap slot, priced fairly.

v3.29.0 — NEW TEXTURES
Long overdue and much-requested. 🚢 Every warship is its own ship now: the Destroyer, Missile Cruiser, Arsenal Ship "Leviathan", Railgun Battlecruiser and Carrier each have a distinct hull instead of all sharing one silhouette — you can finally tell your fleet apart at a glance. 🛩 Distinct drone craft: the combat drone, kamikaze drone, wingman and interceptor now read as different aircraft — and the wingmen are proper pilotless jets, not propeller toys.

v3.28.0 — BOMBARDMENT COUNTERPLAY
The opening orbital bunker-buster barrage was unwinnable without shields — it annihilated every ground position in seconds. Fixed at the root. 🛰 Missiles fall like orbital objects now: the busters are launched IN ORBIT, so they start nearly stationary high in the exosphere and ACCELERATE the whole way down — a descent of several seconds instead of an instant hammer-blow. That's your reaction window. 🎯 Your defenses shoot them down: anti-air and point-defense now track incoming busters and fire LEADING intercept shots at their predicted position — build layered air defense and you can knock most of the barrage out of the sky. Shields are now ONE answer, not the only one. 💥 Pinpoint, not nuclear: a buster is a light, fast penetrator — it kills its one designated target with a small blast, no longer flattening everything in a wide radius. Neglect your air defense and you'll still get hurt — but General and Apocalypse are winnable without shields now.

v3.27.0 — QUALITY OF LIFE
🛰 Garrisons no longer eat orbital lift: a big standing garrison won't lock you out of putting things in orbit — they were already exempt from your army cap, now they're exempt from orbital capacity too. 📱 Smaller strike menu on mobile: the strategic-strike panel now fits comfortably on a phone screen. ⛏ Demolition costs stability: tearing down a building now costs 10 stability on top of the partial IC refund — space management should mean something. 🧱 Denser building: buildings can be packed closer together with slight overlap, so you can fit more into a tight footprint.

v3.26.0 — STABILITY, REFORMED
Stability was a glass jaw — a runaway drain with no counterplay, and an instant game-over. Rebuilt. 🏛 No more death spirals: unstable states (dystopia, superhuman upkeep, dark research) now LOWER your stability CAP instead of bleeding you to zero — a lower ceiling you can rebuild toward with Comms Towers, Propaganda and Radar, never an uncounterable drain. Build enough and you WILL hold. ⚠ Collapse is a crisis, not a coffin: hitting 0 stability no longer ends the game — instead your society seizes up (construction and production freeze, a chunk of your army mutinies and goes inert) while stability claws back. You only fall if you stay pinned at zero for a sustained ~25 seconds. A dip is a scar; total collapse is the end. ⛊ Stability reserve: Comms Towers, Propaganda Bureaus and Radar now bank a stability RESERVE that auto-refills losses (capped at 100) — a shock-absorber you build up in advance. ⛏ Demolition: you can finally tear down your own buildings for a partial IC refund.

v3.25.0 — CLEANUP
🗑 Removed the dispersed launchers: the Mobile Launcher (TEL), the Arsenal Ship strike platform and the Ballistic Submarine are gone — they were buildings pretending to be vehicles, which never quite made sense. Strategic strikes now come from the Missile Silo (bury it to keep it safe). Your naval Arsenal Ship "Leviathan" warship is untouched.

v3.24.0 — INFANTRY SQUADS
Light infantry is no longer a lone soldier — it now deploys as a 4-body SQUAD that moves and thinks as one unit but fights as several. 👥 Four bodies, one brain: three riflemen plus a dedicated AT/AA specialist, each with its own health, weapon and altitude reach — hits land on individual troopers, and the squad fights on (survivors reforming tighter) until the last member falls. 🔫 Burst fire: riflemen fire in short bursts instead of one shot at a time. 🚀 Two layers at once: the specialist independently engages ARMOR and AIRCRAFT while the riflemen handle ground — so a single squad can be shooting a tank and a strike jet in the same breath. ⚡ Lighter on your phone: a squad is ONE simulated entity instead of five, so massed infantry costs a fraction of the performance. Garrisoned infantry become squads automatically.

v3.23.0 — THE GARRISON ECONOMY
A standing homeland-defense force that runs ALONGSIDE your hand-built army — a separate track with its own cap. 🪖 Buildings raise their own garrison: bunkers, barracks, airbases, factories and more now passively fill with standing garrison troops for FREE — you only pay a small IC/s upkeep on what's fielded. 🧱 But mass has a wall: your TOTAL garrison is hard-capped by Garrison Stockpiles (+20 capacity each) — you physically can't garrison past your stockpile budget, so a big standing force costs construction, not just clicks. No more map-filling spam. 🏭 New Infrastructure buildings: Garrison Stockpile (sets the cap), Garrison Factory (adds its own garrison AND speeds nearby buildings' fill), and a cheap Mobilization Hub (fill-speed aura). 📊 New readouts: the top bar now shows your GARRISON and ARMY capacity, each with a live rate. 🗂 Tidying: Rotary Cannon Works and Plasma Bastion Works moved to the Infrastructure tab. Your manually-built army and army cap are completely unchanged — garrison is wholly separate.

v3.22.0 — FIRST CONTACT & A FIERCER FLEET
🎬 Opening cinematic: the game now opens on a typed-out transmission that sets the stakes before the first shot — it plays every launch, and a SKIP appears once you've watched it through once. 💥 Superweapons fight back: the enemy's boss units are no longer passive HP sponges. The LAND LEVIATHAN announces its groundfall with a warning banner and fights with a main plasma gun, a secondary AA turret AND its own air support; the BOMBARDER throws AA micro-missiles and escort sats; the HIVE builds faster and fires a second volley; the ANNIHILATOR gained point-defense; and any boss that survives on the ground long enough calls in one reinforcement wave. (No extra HP or invulnerability — smarter and better-armed, not spongier.) 🛡 Beachhead Shield Generator fixed: it used to self-destruct the instant it landed — now it touches down as a durable, KILLABLE structure that projects its shield dome while it lives; destroy the generator to drop the bubble, and massed fire can no longer delete the dome in a single frame. 🎯 Kinder first matches: the Decapitation bunker-buster barrage now scales to how much air defense you've actually built (a light salvo if you have none, a heavier one if you can shoot them down) instead of a flat wipe. 🗺 Readable minimap: resized to the true proportions of the map — a wide, short strip — so your units finally plot where they really are, in clear color-coded ground / naval / air layers. 📷 Camera stays put: it no longer auto-pans toward threats — the view holds exactly where you leave it. 🎚 New default: BEGIN MOBILIZATION now starts on GENERAL, the most balanced scenario.

v3.21.0 — ATMOSPHERE & FOUNDATIONS
Groundwork for the coming autofleet overhaul. 🌌 The sky is now a real column: the EXOSPHERE — all of space — fills the top HALF of the world, and the THERMOSPHERE is finally its own distinct band beneath it (they used to be one crammed label). ✈ Aircraft are aircraft, not spacecraft: your air force is now hard-capped at the mesosphere. Anything higher — the thermosphere and the vast exosphere — can only be reached by railguns, orbital guns, particle beams, or your own space fleet. Every weapon's altitude reach was re-tuned to the new bands (SAMs still top out in the mesosphere, bunkers in the troposphere, and so on). 🛸 The bulk drones are actual aircraft: the generic combat drone is now a swept delta-wing UAV and the interceptor its own sleek canard fighter, instead of two identical saucers. ⊛ Enemies stop cramming: a wave that used to collapse into a single overlapping stack on a city now spreads into loose groups of distinct craft. 🔧 Research menu fixed: starting a research no longer strands the node overview on-screen with no way to close it (there's now an ✕), and it no longer kills panning on phone (you were left only able to zoom) — plus the view stops yanking back to your era every time you queue something.

v3.20.1 — POST-RELEASE FIXES & ADDITIONS
☢ New strike — Micromissile Barrage: the first research-gated strike — unlock Microrockets and it fires carriers that arc over the target and split into a cloud of independently-homing anti-swarm micro-missiles; cheaper than a nuke, brutal on massed air. 👁 New enemy — EW Jammer: an autodrone that blinds your homing missiles inside its radius — bring dumb-fire or kill it first. 🎯 Air & targeting fixes: fighters can no longer reach orbit (you need railgun / orbital / particle / space weapons to touch space); the multirole Falcon targets correctly; your own micro-missiles no longer chase enemies into orbit; enemy bombers now visibly fire a red point-defense beam at your incoming rounds; and your jets' laser point-defense actually fires now (a short cyan CIWS zap). ⚙ Balance: carriers nerfed (3 → 2 free fighters) and now draw IC/s upkeep; a general late-game unit-upkeep cost so mass has a price; garrisons replenish slower; and enemy beachhead shield domes now survive long enough to actually protect a landing. 🪖 Fix: dug-in emplacements no longer shred your own units with shrapnel when they crumble — an abandoned foxhole just caves in with a puff of dirt. 📱 Mobile: a tappable ❚❚ / ▶ pause button, and the research tree now pinch-zooms and drags with one finger. 📊 Transparency: the top bar shows your influence/s, building cards show the stability-cap they add, and the cost / info menus show unit upkeep.

v3.20.0 — BUG FIXES & COMBAT FEEL
⊕ Fire Control actually works: the ADD TO FIRE CONTROL button did nothing because the info panel was rebuilt every frame, eating the click — fixed, and a fire-control gun now PRIORITIZES your designated targets while still defending on its own when nothing you've marked is in reach (it's never idle). Designating is more forgiving to click. ☄ Weapons: gunfire is now a thin aimed tracer trail instead of a fat scattered ember; artillery shells read as real spun rounds; every weapon kicks a muzzle flash tinted to its type; plasma bolts fly dead straight and AIRBURST next to their target (no more whiffing on movers). 🛡 Shield Generators: the dome ripples across its shell where it's hit and now projects DOWN INTO THE WATER, covering ships. 🔊 Feel: big ground blasts carry a deep sub-bass rumble. 🖥 Hide-HUD: press H for a clean, HUD-free view (movement still works; a hint shows how to bring it back). ◎ Coverage zones: press V or the ◎ button to see radar / fire-rate / repair radii. Plus fixes from playtesting: aircraft no longer explode on empty tanks, music no longer goes quiet in combat, strikes launch when you have the stability for them, and raised terrain no longer strands boats.

v3.19.0 — CONFIRMED LAUNCH & A READABLE MANUAL
☢ Touch strike confirmation: on touch devices a strategic strike now takes two deliberate taps — the first AIMS (the reticle pins where you tapped; tap again to re-aim), then a big ☢ CONFIRM STRIKE / ✕ ABORT bar fires or stands down. No more fat-finger nukes. 📖 FIELD MANUAL reworked: it now opens with a five-step QUICK START, adds a CONTROLS section covering desktop and touch, and every other chapter is a collapsible section you can scan instead of a wall of text — with the economy explained in one place (stability → influence), AIR COMMAND & ORBITAL LIFT documented side by side, and up-to-date strike & fire-control instructions.

v3.18.0 — AIR COMMAND · MOBILE · ACCESSIBILITY
✈ AIR COMMAND fixes aircraft spam: every crewed aircraft now needs a hangar slot — Airbases grant 6, Underground Airwings 3, Aero Works 4; carrier wings support themselves and disposable drones are exempt (swarming is their doctrine). Your air force is capped by real, bombable infrastructure instead of raw money — the PRODUCE header shows ✈ used/total, and it mirrors the orbital-LIFT rule the space fleet already lives by. From the playtest doc: the PRODUCE button now pulses until first use (with a reminder if your factories sit idle), and the moment your first silo finishes, ☢ STRIKE pulses and tells you it's ready — no more finishing a whole campaign without ever finding either. 📱 MOBILE: full touch controls — tap to select/place/fire, one-finger drag to scroll the front, pinch to zoom, long-press to cancel, minimap scrubbing — plus a compact small-screen HUD with finger-sized buttons. ♿ ACCESSIBILITY: the OPTIONS menu grew a dedicated section — Screen Shake toggle, Flash Reduction (dims nuke/muzzle strobes for photosensitivity), Colorblind-Friendly health bars (blue/orange), and a Film Grain & Vignette toggle; all settings (plus UI scale) now SAVE on your device, and the game respects your system's reduced-motion preference out of the box.

v3.17.0 — UNIT GRAPHICS REWORK
The army got a full art pass. Every core unit now carries a proper three-tone paint job — sun-struck upper facets, shaded skirts & undersides, and a coloured identification stripe (cyan for your forces, ember-red on hostiles, applied automatically when drones seize your ground units' colours). Tanks grew commander cupolas, muzzle ends and lit road-wheel hubs; SAMs show their nose cones; the railgun's capacitor bank visibly charges. Things move now: helicopter main & tail rotors actually spin (with a motion-blur disc), the AA track's search radar sweeps, combat-drone rotors whirl, and every jet trails a flickering afterburner flame. Canopies catch a white glint; warships and carriers churn a wake, flash deck markings and blink masthead beacons. The autodrone fleet reads meaner: faceted armour catching the skylight, pulsing hunter-red cores, glowing missile-tube mouths, breathing forge hearts and charged rail tips. Kinetic weapons — cannons, railguns, tank guns — now kick a proper muzzle flash. And the background got fixed too: the parallax ranges are now real jagged mountains (ridged-noise crests with V-cut valleys) wearing snowcaps above the snowline, instead of soft rolling swells.

v3.16.0 — GRAPHICS REWORK
A full visual pass over the whole theatre. The world got deeper: two hazy parallax mountain ranges now roll behind the front line, and the terrain itself grew biome scenery — conifer forests in the wetlands, leafy brush on the plains, dry scrub & pebbles in the deserts, boulders on the rocky heights and glinting snowfields on the peaks (it all keeps clear of your cities). Water is alive: rolling swells, a bright surface crest, drifting sun glints and foam washing at every shoreline. The sky got a ceiling worth scrolling to: a cratered gibbous MOON, slow emerald AURORA curtains rippling through the upper atmosphere, occasional shooting stars through the exosphere, and an anamorphic lens streak on the sun. Combat hits harder on the eyes: explosions now throw glowing EMBERS that arc and gutter out, shockwave rings bloom additively, smoke puffs are lit with a bright crown over a dark body, and young fireballs burn white-hot at the core. The title-screen Earth was remastered too — night-side city lights glitter as continents roll into darkness, the ocean catches a specular sun glint, a sunlit rim wraps the day side, and tiny satellites blink along tilted orbits. A soft vignette frames it all. (Aurora, meteors & planet spin respect the REDUCED MOTION option.) Zoomed-in scrolling fixed: the camera clamps are now zoom-aware, so while zoomed in you can finally pan all the way to the ground, the world's edges and the bottom of the subterranean layer; pan speed matches what the eye sees at any zoom, and the minimap's white viewport box tracks the true visible span.

v3.15.0 — STABILITY ECONOMY REWORK
A big rebalance of the political economy to smooth the difficulty curve. Influence now comes ONLY from Stability — the higher your stability, the faster research & army cap grow. Stability no longer ticks up freely; it climbs slowly toward a STABILITY CAP (shown as cur / cap up top). Comms Towers, Propaganda Bureaus & Radar now raise that CAP instead of granting flat stability/influence. Dangerous-research ⚠ unrest now recovers on its own over time, so you're never permanently walled out. Fixes: your own Mind-Forge plasma column no longer fries your own troops; Arsenal Ships / Ballistic Subs now build at the water surface instead of briefly appearing on the seabed. Fire Control got a full Field Manual entry (open the manual) — it works; it just needed explaining.

v3.14.0 — GLOBAL PROJECTILES & CLEARER GUNS
Projectiles now live everywhere on the map, not just near your camera — battles on a far front fully resolve even while you're watching somewhere else (shells, missiles, rail slugs and rockets used to be culled off-screen). Also clarified the Fire Control guns: select a heavy gun (Bunker, Laser Tower, Orbital Gun, Mass Driver, Microrocket Battery, Particle Cannon), hit ⊕ ADD TO FIRE CONTROL, then click incoming enemies inside its radar to designate them — the gun then fires only at what you mark (right-click / Esc releases). Stale "manual control" wording on a few guns was corrected to match.

v3.13.1 — BUG FIXES
Fixes from an independent code review: explosions near a city no longer damage it from high altitude (blast splash now respects vertical distance to city districts, like it already did for units); the research detail panel shows each building's real artwork instead of a generic factory box; and the research tech-tree time estimate now accounts for game speed.

v3.13.0 — AFTER-ACTION REPORT
Polish pass: winning or losing now ends on a proper battle summary instead of a bare title. The victory/defeat screen tallies drones destroyed, waves repelled, cities held, districts & forces lost, and time in combat, topped with a performance commendation (hold every city untouched for a ★★★ Flawless Defense). Gives each battle a real payoff and a score to beat.

v3.12.0 — DEFLECTOR TECH PATH
Deflector Shields is now a combination of the Point Defense and Directed Energy upgrades — it sits downstream of both on the research tree and requires you to have researched each before you can unlock the Shield Generator. A deflector field is the fusion of an interceptor's targeting and a beam weapon's projector tech, so the path now reflects that.

v3.11.0 — CAMERA & UI
Two quality-of-life controls. Zoom: roll the mouse wheel (or use the +/−/⌂ buttons, bottom-right) to zoom in toward the cursor and back out — get right down on your units to watch them fight, or pull back to the full view. (Shift+wheel still pans the tall sky vertically.) Minimize the build bar: the ⚙ BUILD header now has a ▾ arrow that collapses the whole build panel down to a small tab so it's out of your way — click ▸ to bring it back.

v3.10.0 — DEFENSE & DESTRUCTION
The rod apocalypse has answers now. A new DEFENSE research line: Point Defense (Aegis Battery — rapid flak that swats incoming missiles & tungsten rods), Microrockets (rockets that split into several INDEPENDENTLY-homing submunitions — re-arms your strike aircraft & unlocks the Microrocket Battery), and Deflector Shields (Shield Generators that dome your forces — rods, missiles & bombs splash off them until battered down, then recharge). Plus Particle Beams off the energy line — Particle Cannons fire single hypervelocity bolts that punch through anything at any altitude. And dispersed ballistic platforms — a road-mobile Launcher (TEL), an offshore Arsenal Ship and a Ballistic Submarine — so your strike arsenal isn't all in one silo waiting to be glassed; plant them in important spots.
Enemies now break apart by what kills them: lasers slag & drop them intact; guns leave them smoking & riddled before they fall; missiles pop and tumble out of the sky; plasma blows the body off the shot with spall trailing behind; railguns & particle bolts split them clean in half with a debris cloud. Explosions got a bright bloom and leave black smoke rising to fill the sky.
Fixes: tungsten-rod bombardment now rains on cities & your infrastructure across the WHOLE map — no longer just wherever your camera is looking; and the Cluster MIRV now reliably splits at the top of its arc instead of occasionally fizzling. The Mass-Driver Railway moved down to Orbital Operations (earlier access).

v3.9.0 — FIRE CONTROL
Manual gun control is now a real fire-direction system. Select a heavy gun and hit ⊕ ADD TO FIRE CONTROL — then select others and add them too, building a whole battery under your command. The group projects a radar over its combined range (range rings + a sweeping scope), and you click each incoming enemy to designate it as a target — designated foes get a spinning target reticle, and every gun in the group automatically engages the marked targets that fall within its reach (so high-altitude designations are taken by your railguns & orbital guns, ground ones by your bunkers). Click a target again to drop it; right-click or Esc releases the whole battery. Designate the tungsten rod streaking toward your capital and watch the whole line swing onto it. Also: the Mass-Driver Railway moved down to Orbital Operations — it's now an early long-range emplacement, no Orbital Command research required.

v3.8.0 — PRODUCTION CHAINS
Your biggest units are now ASSEMBLED from a real industrial chain, not conjured from raw IC. Two new component parts — Heavy Alloy (poured by Factories, faster by the Heavy Foundry) and Rocket Parts (built by Space Centers & Space Stations) — accumulate in stock over time, and you SPEND them to build the big stuff: Heavy & Super-Heavy tanks cost alloy; every orbital unit costs rocket parts. Orbital units also need ORBITAL LIFT capacity — each Space Center provides 5 lift (a Space Station +8) and every satellite/frigate/dreadnought reserves some while it's in orbit, so a larger space fleet means building more launch infrastructure (the "needs N orbital capacity to lift" rule). And Special Resources are now true enablers, not just discounts: the Railgun needs a STEEL deposit to build at all — claim the ground that has what your war machine runs on. The PRODUCE panel shows your live lift & parts, each unit card lists what it consumes (greying out when you're short), and the 📊 STATS panel tracks your stockpiles.

v3.7.0 — TAKE THE TRIGGER
You can now take manual control of your heavy guns. Select a Bunker, Laser Tower, Nanite Turret, Orbital Gun or Mass-Driver Railway and hit ⊕ MANUAL CONTROL — the gun stops firing on its own and hands you the trigger: a dashed aim line follows your cursor to a targeting reticle, and you click to fire wherever you point (it still has to reload between shots). Snipe a descending dropship out of the exosphere, walk railgun rounds across a landing, or hold fire and pick your moment. Right-click or Esc (or ⊗ RELEASE) gives the gun back to the AI. The autonomous war keeps running around you — manual control is opt-in, per emplacement, exactly when you want your own hands on a weapon.

v3.6.0 — THE LIVING SKY
A graphics & atmosphere overhaul. The sky now reads as real, layered atmosphere: deep black space at the very top, a drifting nebula and a richer, twinkling, multi-coloured starfield up high, a soft sun glowing in the upper sky, and distinct colour bands flowing down through the mesosphere, stratosphere and troposphere to a warm, glowing horizon that hugs the curved planetary limb. The ground has depth now — layered rock strata and mineral speckle in the subterranean body, exposed ore veins glinting beneath every resource deposit, and a sun-lit topsoil edge. Clouds are fuller and shaded with sunlit crests. And every unit now casts a soft drop-shadow (plus a ground contact shadow), so your forces read clearly against the brightest sky or the blackest space. The world finally looks like the curved, colourful atmospheric battlefield it was always meant to be.

v3.5.0 — TOTAL WAR
A huge combat & systems batch. Point-defence overhaul: CIWS and ALL PD turrets now shoot down incoming enemy MISSILES, not just tungsten rods. Armed populace: every building now defends itself at close range (rifles by default), and cities are fortified and fire back — build a Rotary Cannon Works to upgrade every building & city to CIWS-class rapid flak + missile interception, or a Plasma Bastion Works (Plasma Weapons) for heavy plasma cannons everywhere. Occupied cities stop being shelled and instead get fortified with massive immobile SIEGE GUNS that hammer you (clear them to retake). City losses bite: an occupied city bleeds stability until you retake it, and every destroyed city structure is a PERMANENT stability hit. Underground isn't safe: earthquakes rapidly cave in buried structures, bombs & heavy rounds crack SHALLOW tunnels, and enemies that overrun a buried building breach it (deep buildings resist far more). Combat Drop: a new strategic command deploys YOUR OWN squad anywhere — paratroopers → drop-pods → orbital landings as the ages advance. Scenario Editor (SCENARIOS → ⚙ CUSTOM) lets you dial prep time, difficulty, fleet size, orbital bombardment, ground intensity, skyfall and which superweapons appear, then launch a custom invasion. Hovering a research node or special building now previews its stability impact on the stability readout. Enemy aircraft now weave & bob like real aircraft; antimatter WHISTLER drones lob a finite pool of tiny antimatter rounds, then (or once wounded) dive into a target and detonate; aircraft rearm far faster; enemy drops avoid landing dead-centre in cities; underground hangars cost ~half and burying already-underground buildings (rail hubs, forges, hangars) no longer costs extra; ships no longer get shoved onto land. Plus an achievements framework (🏆 in the footer) ready for medals to come.

v3.4.0 — THE TALL SKY
The skybox is now genuinely TALL — the world is ~1.9× the height of your screen, so the atmosphere stretches from deep black space at the very top, down through the mesosphere, stratosphere and troposphere to the ground far below. The camera now pans VERTICALLY as well as horizontally: it auto-follows the action (sitting on the ground fight by default, rising to frame high-altitude threats when the sky is the battlefield), and you can take manual control any time with W/S, ↑/↓, the mouse wheel, or the top/bottom screen edges. Re-entry now reads as a real plunge — a dropship takes the better part of ten seconds to fall the whole way down, giving your exosphere-reaching weapons (railguns, lasers, orbital guns, satellites) a long window to shoot it apart before it ever lands. Orbital lances and the deep-space stars, space-elevator tether and layer guides all live in their proper place in the much bigger sky.

v3.3.1 — BOMBARDMENT RULES
Orbital bombardment is now reserved for the heavy intents. A Probing Attack (Recruit) and a Decapitation Strike (Officer) no longer rain orbital ordnance at all — a probe is just a ground & air feeler, and a decapitation is a precision capital drop, not a barrage. Only a FULL INVASION (General / "total war") and ORBITAL ANNIHILATION (Apocalypse / glassing) bring the falling bombpods and tungsten-rod barrage. So the lighter difficulties are about holding the line against landings, and the orbital sky-fire is the signature of the worst two.

v3.3.0 — HOSTILE TAKEOVER
The autodrones now read as the enemy: every ENEMY GROUND unit (landed tanks, walkers, pelters, earthbreakers, shield strikers, the Land Leviathan) is repainted a reddish dark-grey so you can tell hostile armour from your own at a glance. A captured city is no longer just a flag — when a region falls, the enemy SEIZES the factories, plants and industry inside it and turns your own war economy against you: those buildings stop producing for you (no output, no garrison) and start spitting out enemy ground forces, marked with a red "◗ SEIZED" flag. Retake the region with ground troops to bring your industry back online. SMARTER TARGETING: turrets and units now de-conflict their fire — before committing a shot they check how much fire is already inbound on a target, so a line of laser/flak turrets spreads across an incoming barrage instead of dumping ten shots into one tungsten rod and letting the rest through (big upgrade for point-defence vs. orbital lances). All weapons also fire with a small randomized timing jitter (up to ±0.3s) so a formation no longer fires in robotic lock-step. WARSHIPS got a cleaner hull — a sleeker, less-blocky silhouette with a raked bow, faceted stealth superstructure and flush VLS.

v3.2.1 — FORTIFY
INFANTRY are stronger (more HP, harder-hitting) and now genuinely earn their keep: a dug-in ground unit AUTO-BUILDS its own emplacements — MG nests, flak/AA nests and field-gun artillery — so a held line grows into a real mini-fort (the emplacements crumble if the unit dies or marches off). STABILITY OFFSET reworked per request: dangerous research now PERMANENTLY lowers stability — it does NOT auto-heal. The only way to recover it is running stability-boosting STRUCTURES (Comms Towers, Radar, and the new PROPAGANDA BUREAU which strongly raises stability). So a late-game research spree quietly kneecaps your stability → influence → research speed unless you invest in keeping the populace in line. New POINT-DEFENCE: the CIWS "Sentry" — a cheap rotary-autocannon turret (no research) that throws a wall of flak to shoot down incoming bombs/missiles and intercept falling TUNGSTEN RODS & orbital lances. Screen your cities with them.

v3.2.0 — DOCTRINE BALANCE
A pass to make the non-laser/plasma paths pull their weight, plus difficulty pacing. PREP TIME is now set by the fleet's intent: a Probing strike gives you only 200s, a Decapitation the usual 135s, a Full Invasion a long 450s, and Annihilation a full 500s to dig in. MECHANICAL & vat-grown units (drones, androids, mechs, satellites, clones) no longer count against your army cap — only manpower-crewed units do, so synthetic armies can swarm. STABILITY OFFSET is back: dangerous research now costs a recoverable unrest offset that decays over ~10s (shown as ⚠ on the stability readout) instead of a permanent loss — riskier doctrines sting, then heal. New NANITE TURRET (Nanotech) fires nanobot rounds that disassemble heavy armour — a strong defensive line off the nanotech path, no Nanite Foundry needed. ENTRENCHMENT: ground units that hold position dig in for a damage-reduction bonus, and standing in a building's footprint (especially an economic block or bunker) GARRISONS it for deep cover — build your own mini-forts. Airbases now keep a mixed air patrol (interceptors + strike jets + helis), and special-resource buildings field a small thematic garrison (cloning vats → clones, gene facility → shock troops, drone line → combat drones, etc.). Retextured the Stealth, Laser Plane, Heavy Bomber and Strike Jet so they no longer share sprites.

v3.1.2 — THE FLEET ROSTER
Five new autodrone units straight off the fleet sketches. The AUTODRONE BOMBARDER — a colossal high-orbit capital fabricator that hangs in the exosphere raining orbital ordnance, birthing drones, and swatting your shots out of the air with point-defence (only space-reaching weapons can touch it). The CONSTANT THREAT bulwark — an exosphere heavy-armour platform that lobs nuke-calibre plasma down onto your cities; ground missiles can't even reach it. The PELTER — a ground plasma-artillery turret dropped in swarms, constant pressure on your cities. The EARTHBREAKER PRESS — a heavy seismic siege unit whose energy field triggers earthquakes that rattle morale (stability) and shake apart nearby ground forces & buildings. And the beachhead shield carrier is now the proper SHIELD STRIKER droppod — on touchdown it raises its dome AND disgorges a ground squad like an armoured command centre (still vulnerable on the way down — shoot it before it lands). Each has its own silhouette.

v3.1.1 — ORBIT & RE-ENTRY
Orbital units now PATROL the exosphere band like aircraft — cruising the orbit and weaving onto targets instead of sitting still. RE-ENTRY is far slower now: the fleet begins a long, vulnerable high-altitude descent and only gradually accelerates as it bites into thicker air — giving your exosphere-reaching units (railguns, laser towers, orbital sats, high aircraft) real time to start shooting it down before it ever goes active. And the beachhead SHIELD now drops as a CARRIER alongside its wave — it only raises the dome once it touches down, so you get a window to shoot the carrier out of the sky and deny the shield entirely.

v3.1.0 — DOCTRINE PASS
PURPOSE-BUILT AIRCRAFT: interceptors (Falcon / Wraith / Solaris) are AIR-SUPERIORITY only now — they can't strike ground. For ground attack you build the new Strike Jet "Warthog" or fly Gunships / Helis / Bombers (which hit ground & low air, not high fighters). MISSILE aircraft now carry a finite magazine and fly back to an AIRBASE or CARRIER to rearm — so the sky isn't an endless missile barrage and your ground units get their moment (watch the yellow ammo bar). Enemy WAVES now hit as ONE concentrated LANDING instead of scattered random drops, and ground beachheads throw up a radial SHIELD DOME you must batter down before you can hit what's under it. WATER now stops most ground units at the shoreline (orbital drops can still splash down — enemy armor rides the surface, amphibious) and aircraft no longer dip into the sea. Distinct ORBITAL sprites: the Orbital Frigate is a real armoured warship hull, the Strike Fighter & Missile Sat each got their own look (no more sat-clones).

v3.0.0 — THE 3.0 UPDATE (pt.2)
AUTODRONE SUPERWEAPONS: the Skyfortress "Hive" (flying drone-carrier that births a swarm), the Land Leviathan (siege crawler that grinds toward your cities), and the Orbital Annihilator (hangs in orbit and drops a glassing column on your cities — only high-reach weapons can kill it). They arrive on the fleet's intent schedule with boss HP bars; killing one steadies the nation. Ground forces can now CAPTURE cities (a capture meter you reverse with your own ground troops) — the minimap shows a ground FRONTLINE. New TERRAIN tool: smooth RAISE / LEVEL / SINK brushes (no more jagged carves), and buildings sit on a poured FOUNDATION so you can build on uneven ground (no more "cannot build here"). Much TALLER skybox; cities have distinct paved ground. SPEC tab lists your active special-resource buffs, and a 📊 STATS panel shows every current stat.

v2.7.0 — COMBAT & INVASION OVERHAUL (3.0 pt.1)
PLASMA reworked: it's a contained KINETIC SLUG now — fired dead straight & fast (no more useless homing curl), remodelled as a hot tracer dart, and it dumps its heat & SPALLS hard on contact (real impact + screen kick). Low power = quick light bolts, high power = heavy arcing tank/arty slugs. Plasma only re-arms GUN units — missile units (interceptors, stealth, helis, SAMs) KEEP their missiles, which are also smaller now. Combat feels WEIGHTY: armor of all kinds nerfed, hits buffed, every wreck throws shrapnel & kicks the screen, bigger dramatic explosions. Difficulty is now the autofleet's INTENT: Recruit=probing recon · Officer=decapitation strike on your capital · General=full invasion with a mass SKYFALL drop + flank ground landings · Apocalypse=orbital ANNIHILATION (no landing, they just glass you). New enemy GROUND armor & walkers. Idle ground units no longer freeze — they march to the fight.

v2.6.0 — IMMERSION PASS
The Mantle Forge now auto-buries itself to the deep layer (its build card shows the dug cost). The Space Station puts an actual platform up in the exosphere, tethered by a space elevator with a climber bead. Carrier wings now fly out, spend their ordnance, then return to land on the deck, rearm, and re-launch.

v2.5.0 — PRODUCTION LINES
New PROD buildings add whole new unit types to your factories with no research — a parallel path to the tech tree. Missile Works → the "Hydra" rocket battery; Heavy Foundry → the "Mammoth" super-heavy tank; Aero Works → the "Lancer" heavy bomber (and it also lets you build Laser Planes natively). Locked units now show a "🏭 build a …" hint in the production menu telling you which line unlocks them, and once the line is up they light up green (NEW · via <building>).
